TASK-001.gold_answer: A qualifying SBIR awardee must generally be a U.S.-based for-profit small business, satisfy the applicable U.S. ownership and control requirements, and have no more than 500 employees including affiliates.

TASK-002.gold_answer: No. A nonprofit organization cannot directly receive an SBIR or STTR award. A nonprofit may participate in certain other permitted roles, including as a subcontractor or qualifying STTR research institution.

TASK-003.gold_answer: At least 40 percent of the R&D work must be performed by the small business and at least 30 percent must be performed by the partnering research institution.

TASK-004.gold_answer: No. Under the normal SBIR Phase I performance-of-work requirement, a minimum of two-thirds of the research or analytical effort must be performed by the awardee.

TASK-006.gold_answer: No. An NSF Phase I proposer must first submit a Project Pitch and receive an official invitation from NSF program staff before submitting the full proposal.

TASK-007.gold_answer: No. Only NSF Phase I SBIR/STTR awardees may submit an NSF Phase II proposal. The Phase II proposal must be submitted between 6 and 24 months after the start date of the relevant NSF Phase I award.

TASK-008.gold_answer: Normally no. NSF defines primary employment as at least 51 percent employment with the small business and normally considers employment elsewhere exceeding 19.6 hours per week to conflict with this requirement. Twenty-five hours per week with another employer therefore normally conflicts with the requirement.

TASK-013.gold_answer: Insufficient evidence. The supplied records establish some relevant facts about Galois, including U.S. location, reported employee count, and prior SBIR participation, but they do not conclusively establish every current ownership, control, affiliation, and other eligibility condition required for a new SBIR award.
